source.title: Reductive Elimination of H2 Activates Nitrogenase to Reduce the N≡N Triple Bond: Characterization of the E4(4H) Janus Intermediate in Wild-Type Enzyme
source.authors: Lukoyanov D, Khadka N, Yang ZY, Dean DR, Seefeldt LC, Hoffman BM
source.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
source.inspection: Retained primary main-manuscript XML: Methods P11-P13; WT state-assignment and cryoannealing discussion P14, P20 and P32-P35; source-model summary P41; Figures 3, 4 and 9 captions; Chart 3 XML reference. The Figure 9 and Chart 3 raster assets and cited earlier-method papers were not inspected in this projection.

constructs.identity: Source-named wild-type Azotobacter vinelandii MoFe protein prepared under the paper's cited expression and purification procedure.
constructs.scope: Source-reported WT construct identity only; exact sequence, strain, plasmid, purification batch and physical specimen identity are not established from the selected retained primary XML.

assays.endpoint: Two source-assigned E4-state EPR signal-amplitude progress curves during post-turnover frozen-solid cryoannealing
assays.method: Turnover freeze-quench followed by cryoannealing and intermittent continuous-wave EPR state-signal readout

preparation.scope: The selected main text supplies these X-band sample and Figure 9 conditions. Complete turnover chemistry and preparation details remain in cited earlier procedures and are not reconstructed here.

annealing.source_basis: P32 states that keeping the sample frozen abolishes reduced-Fe-protein binding and oxidized-Fe-protein release, preventing additional reducing-equivalent accumulation during relaxation.
annealing.scope: A nonturnover cryoannealing phase applied after turnover and freeze-quench; it is not a physiological turnover time course.

readout.measurement: EPR signal amplitude at the well-resolved g1 features of the E4 states

E4_2N2H.assignment_scope: Source-assigned FeMo-co S = 1/2 nitrogenous state at the diazene-reduction level; exact structure and coordination geometry are unknown.

E4_4H.assignment_scope: The paper assigns the WT signal to Janus with two bridging hydrides using its EPR, ENDOR and photophysical evidence; exact Fe-pair and complete protonation geometry are not established.

E4_4H_EPR_conditions.source_basis: Figure 9 states that E4(4H) spectra use the Figure 4 EPR conditions.

readout.other_state_EPR_conditions: Figure 9 refers E4(2N2H), E2 and E0 conditions and quantitation procedures to an earlier study that is not part of this retained projection.
readout.E4_concentration_scaling: Figure 9 states that E4-state intensities were converted to concentration units by scaling the three-step kinetic scheme for the corresponding decays.
readout.scope: The direct readout is state-assigned EPR signal amplitude. Molecular-state abundance, nitrogen release and hydrogen addition are not directly observed by EPR.

assays.scope: One shared WT low-N2 H2O frozen-mixture experiment with two selected E4-state progress curves; the two state records are not independent experiments.

state_time_course.source_token: The E4(2N2H) EPR signal amplitude was monitored across the Figure 9 cryoannealing progress curve.
state_time_course.scope: One source-reported monitored state-signal trajectory in the shared four-state frozen-sample experiment. This record carries no encoded direction, absolute concentration series, independent replicate, transition chemistry or elementary rate.

state_time_course.source_token: The E4(4H) Janus EPR signal amplitude was monitored across the same Figure 9 cryoannealing progress curve.
state_time_course.scope: One source-reported monitored state-signal trajectory in the shared four-state frozen-sample experiment. This record carries no encoded direction, net-rise assertion, absolute concentration series, independent replicate, transition chemistry or elementary rate.

source_assessment.observed: Figure 9 reports jointly monitored time courses for four EPR-detected, source-assigned states during cryoannealing. The two selected E4 observations retain only that monitored signal-amplitude scope.

state_assignments.E4_2N2H: The source assigns the g1 = 2.09 signal to an FeMo-co S = 1/2 E4(2N2H) state at the diazene-reduction level. Figure 3 explicitly leaves its structure and coordination geometry unknown.
state_assignments.E4_4H: The source assigns the g1 = 2.15 WT signal to E4(4H) Janus with two bridging hydrides on the basis of the paper's EPR, ENDOR and photophysical evidence.

author_model_interpretation.relation: P35 interprets loss of E4(2N2H) through H2 oxidative addition as kinetically coupled to formation of E4(4H), and P41 places that relation at the start of a sequential frozen-state relaxation pathway.
author_model_interpretation.source_assigned_chemistry: oxidative addition of H2 with release of N2
author_model_interpretation.evidence_status: author interpretation of jointly monitored, source-assigned EPR progress curves under the fitted sequential model; not a directly observed bond-making, gas-release or atom-resolved event

source_assessment.downstream_drain: The same source model continues E4(4H) through E2 to E0 during cryoannealing. Janus is therefore modeled as both formed and consumed, and the retained text does not by itself establish that the net E4(4H) signal rises over any interval.
source_assessment.concentration_scaling: The E4 measurements begin as EPR signal intensities; Figure 9 says their conversion to concentration units scales the three-step kinetic scheme. Absolute E4 concentrations and fitted starting populations are therefore model-dependent and are not projected here.
source_assessment.fit_scope: The source permits distributed kinetics for the first two fitted relaxation steps and an exponential third step. Reported time constants and stretch parameters describe fitted frozen-sample relaxation phases, not elementary microscopic rate constants, and are not projected here.

figure_witness.impact: P34-P35 support the qualitative source-model coupling. The absent raster witnesses block independent curve-shape and color verification, any net-Janus-rise claim, and assignment of the caption's individual fit parameters to specific arrows.

limitations: The two E4 records are co-observed state-signal time courses from one shared frozen-mixture experiment, not two independent experiments or a pairwise perturbation comparison.
EPR detects signal amplitudes; the E4 labels, nitrogenous/hydride composition and state-to-state chemistry retain their source-assignment or author-model status.
The retained XML does not include the Figure 9 or Chart 3 raster. No curve digitization, direction-specific Janus observation, color-to-state reconstruction or fit-parameter-to-arrow mapping is made.

Reported relaxation time constants, stretch parameters and fitted state populations are not projected. They must not be treated as elementary rates, kinetic constants transferable to turnover, or independently calibrated concentrations.
Cryoannealing is a post-turnover frozen-solid intervention. It does not establish the time course, rate or population relation during physiological turnover.

Exact sequence, strain, physical preparation, complete turnover mixture, turnover temperature, biological replicate count and EPR conditions for all four states remain unresolved in this retained scope.
No direct N2 release, H2 addition, exact Fe/S sites, complete protonation state, productive geometry, source-step/M0212 correspondence, new project experiment or independent human validation follows.
